title: The screening's capacity under production limits (audit #53 part 1; the founder's rulings of 2026-10-20, decisions 13 to 16, and of 2026-10-21, Q1 (a), Q7 and Q8)
assertion: The production images at production's task sizes, the screening consumer among them (WORKER_JOBS=screening at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, three threads, on its own login) beside a platform that prices none, Postgres at db.t4g.medium's 2 vCPU on the runner's first CPUs with gp3's baseline and a 2 ms round trip, the SYNTHETIC scale release (2.2 million records): the practice and worst 50,000-row uploads alone and three at once (cold, the worst ones distinct, each upload a prospect of its own) with a small one sent once the large uploads' jobs are queued; fails on an OOM kill (Postgres's included), a restart, anonymous memory above 90% of a limit (the consumer's included), a limit or cold start not applied, the consumer measured at another size than declared or its threads not pricing at once (a free thread takes the next normal job at once: each send to a screening queue wakes the consumer's workers through LISTEN/NOTIFY and each run's end wakes them again, pg-boss's 2-s poll kept as the fallback), a runner too small (fewer than 4 CPUs), a wrong, unfinished or stalled result, a result page that does not open (its first page of groups or its last), a small upload not queued behind the large ones, the platform pricing a screening, a process-runtime layout missing what the images hold (PROCESS_IMAGES_INCOMPLETE), an upload in the waiting tier, the consumer's time to email not logged or out of its bounds (never above the time from the harness's click to its own line, never more than 2 s below the harness's, the web's receipt stamped by its proxy before the body is read), a request that left for the static origin, an oracle mismatch or an oracle short of an upload's Medicare rows (S1-1, S2-1 and S3-1 against the read and adapter frozen at 3c1b289, and S1-2, a ZIP the release splits across localities sent with its ZIP+4, against the whole-release oracle), or a run of fewer than S1 to S5; time enforced: any upload above 48 s on the runner fails (60 s scaled by the runner-to-Fargate factor once staging measures it), and a worst time above 44 s goes to the founder as a sizing question, shown on the pull request's checks as a warning; required on every pull request through a gate that runs even after a cancel and measures when a path of the derived watched list changed (the import closure of the screening's entry points and the files no import reaches, held equal to what watched.ts derives); the release loader analyzes and freezes rule_record after a load, and the keyed read probes the index per key (operator_screening_run_keys estimated at one row)
noFileReason: The capacity test builds its SYNTHETIC scale release and uploads outside the repository when it runs; no file is committed.
